questionText: How do you implement consistent error responses in Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can design, implement, and test one safe ProblemDetail error contract across expected domain failures, Spring MVC failures, security failures, and unexpected errors.
inScope: Shared exception translation with RestControllerAdvice and ExceptionHandler
Ownership of domain, MVC, security, and unexpected failure paths
Safe public details and protected diagnostics
A complete integration-tested not-found handler fixture
Focused learner-facing handler and web-layer contract assertions

claims.statement: RestControllerAdvice combines controller advice with response-body handling, and its ExceptionHandler methods can translate exceptions across controllers into HTTP responses.
ResponseEntityExceptionHandler is a convenient controller-advice base class for handling Spring MVC exceptions and ErrorResponseException values with problem-detail response bodies.
In Spring Boot 3.3, setting spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true enables Problem Details support for built-in Spring MVC exceptions.
RFC 9457 defines the problem-detail members type, status, title, detail, and instance, and permits extension members for problem-specific data.

When Spring MVC renders ProblemDetail, its status determines the HTTP status, the current request path can supply instance when absent, and problem JSON or XML media types are favored for content negotiation.
Spring ProblemDetail supports non-standard properties and its Jackson mix-in renders properties-map entries as top-level JSON members.

Authentication and authorization failures can be handled by Spring Security before a controller method, so their entry-point and access-denied responses need deliberate alignment with the API error contract.
The public response must use an HTTP status whose defined meaning matches the failure, such as 404 for an absent target, 409 for a current-state conflict, or 500 for an unexpected server failure.

examples.title: Complete fixture for a focused ProblemDetail handler and MockMvc contract

validation.command: Run mvn -q test with Java 17 in an isolated Spring Boot 3.3.1 fixture containing the complete advice, exception, controller, configuration, and MockMvc test
validation.expected: The fixture compiles and two MockMvc checks pass: the custom missing-order handler returns the documented 404 problem contract, and the enabled built-in MVC support returns a 400 problem response for an invalid path-variable conversion

visuals.title: Security, MVC, and domain failures converging on one public problem contract and protected diagnostics

notes: The lesson describes one simple domain handler without implying that one catch-all method should own every framework and security error path.
The lesson separates safe public recovery information from protected exception diagnostics.
Learners see only the relevant handler and assertion lines; the evidence check used a complete isolated fixture with imports, supporting types, application configuration, controller, and test setup.

review.notes: Spring error-response behavior was checked against official Spring Boot 3.3.1, Spring Framework, and Spring Security documentation; problem fields were checked against RFC 9457 and status mappings against RFC 9110. The complete Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.3.1 fixture passed two MockMvc contract tests, and the ownership flow matches the documented boundaries.
